name: Valorant
notes: Yaw is fixed at 0.07. FOV is 103 horizontal at 16:9 (about 70.5 vertical) with the vertical angle kept for other aspect ratios; these FOV values come from community sources, not Riot documentation. Trainer geometry (the `trainer` block) is an assumption, not a measurement, except the values taken from open-aim (commit 807f557, M23, docs/VALORANT-WEIGHTS.md): the `body` and `movement` blocks, the click-target distances (`clickTargetDistanceQuantiles`, heads of 0.24 m), the flick angle bins (offsets from the crosshair in open-aim's flash drills: 18 / 21 / 24 / 18 / 19 percent up to 5 / 10 / 20 / 40 / 90 degrees) and the off-level share. Open-aim drills show what players train, not match frequencies. Strafing at 3-6 m/s is still an assumption. Riot publishes no hitbox or speed numbers; measure them in the shooting range (docs/history/REVIEW.md, Realism) and set verified to true.

clickTargetDistanceQuantiles.source: open-aim commit 807f557, flash drills (18 scenes, 260 exposure points), extracted by tools/openaim-extract into valorant-engagements.json (groups.flash.metrics.distance, p5-p95 and max). The minimum 4.0 m is an assumption: the measured minimum 1.63 m is a single spawn next to the player, and a head that close (8 degrees) is not a flick target. Drills show what players train, not how often a distance occurs in a match; Riot reports that nearly half of Phantom kills are within 15 m (this curve: 32 percent). With these distances the click targets are heads of the body block (0.24 m), so clickTargetDiameterDegrees and clickTargetDistanceMeters are not used (docs/VALORANT-WEIGHTS.md section 6).

elevation.notes: Assumption, not a measurement. Valorant maps are mostly flat and players place the crosshair at head height, so most enemies are within about 1.5 degrees of the crosshair level; about 12 percent are on a different level (heaven positions, ramps, stairs, crouching players), 3-10 degrees up or down, more of them above. M23: offLevelShare 0.27 is the share of open-aim flash-drill exposures (commit 807f557, valorant-engagements.json) with more than 1.5 degrees of elevation (bootstrap CI 13-42 percent); the other values are still assumptions. Riot publishes no eye height, head height or map elevation statistics (secondary sources only say all agents are about 2 m tall); eye and head centre are both 1.75 m (the `body` block), so level targets are exactly level. Measure in the shooting range (docs/history/REVIEW.md, Realism) and set verified to true.

arena.notes: The far wall stands behind the farthest click target (60.3 m, clickTargetDistanceQuantiles). Corners and doorways keep the defaults.

flash.notes: Documented windups (PC): Flashpoint 0.5 s, Arc Rose 0.5 s, Curveball 0.6 s, Blindside 0.6 s (the quick, common flashes; KAY/O FLASH/drive 1.0 s lobbed or 1.6 s thrown and Skye Guiding Light up to 2 s are slower and not modelled); maximum blind 1.5 s (Curveball, Blindside) to 2.25 s. Players who look away are blinded only briefly (secondary sources). The time a flash is visible before it pops also contains part of its flight, which no source gives: popDelaySeconds 0.5-0.65 follows the common windups (the visible flight before the windup is not given by any source); an earlier 0.45-0.9 was found too slow by the player and was chosen so that the simulated hand neither always nor never turns away in time. The exit margin of 10 degrees past the edge of the screen is an assumption for the glare. Measure both in the shooting range and set verified to true.

spawnDelaySeconds.source: Measured, rough: clips of 2026-10-22 (60 fps, one played run, n = 19): a new bot about 1.8 s after the previous spawn minus a shot bot's lifetime of 1.4 s gives about 0.4 s; the 0.2-0.8 s spread is an assumption.

speedPresets.source: Assumption, not measured: the range has Speed Easy / Medium / Hard (valorant.fandom.com/wiki/Range) but none was selected in the clips; a bot lives 3.0 / 2.0 / 1.2 s. Without a preset an unshot bot never leaves (measured: one stayed 44 s).

bearingDegrees.source: Measured: clips of 2026-10-22, bearings -51 to +81 degrees from the counter's forward direction in a played run; uniform between them is an assumption.

distanceMeters.source: Measured, rough: 3-19 m, median 6.8 m, from the angular size of a bot assumed 1.8 m tall (so partly circular); 5-20 m log-uniform is the rounded assumption.

botHeightMeters.source: Derived from the body block (M23): head centre at the standing eye height 1.75 m plus the head radius 0.12 m, so the top of the head is at 1.87 m. Before M23 an assumed 1.8 m.

headDiameterMeters.source: From the body block (M23): open-aim's head sphere, r 0.12 m. Riot publishes no hitbox; before M23 an assumed 0.25 m.

strafe.source: Measured, then adjusted by the player's feel: clips of 2026-10-22 gave move-stop-move with moving segments 0.36 s median (0.25-0.5), stops 0.2 s (0.1-0.3) and about 12 degrees per second at an assumed 12 m (2.5 m/s, so partly circular). The player found the bots in the first version (2.5 m/s, stops 0.1-0.3 s) moving too much and turning too fast, so the values are 2.2 m/s, moves 0.25-0.45 s and stops 0.3-0.7 s (about 40 % of the time moving); after the second play (2026-10-24) the bots were still a touch too fast, so the speed is 2.0 m/s. The reverse probability 0.6 and the +-2 m limit are assumptions.

killRule.source: Assumption: a head hit kills; Vandal damage against 100 health plus 50 armor needs 4 body hits with bot armor on and 3 with it off (Bot Armor is a setting of the range panel). Not observable in the clips.

headDiameterMeters.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): head hit sphere radius 0.12 m (plus two head capsules of radius 0.11 m). Riot publishes no hitbox.

capsuleHeightMeters.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): player capsule halfHeight 0.98 m, radius 0.42 m, so 1.96 m tall. Secondary sources say agents are about 2 m tall.

eyeStandMeters.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): eye height 1.75 m standing; open-aim also puts the head centre of a bot there.

eyeCrouchMeters.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): eye height 1.35 m crouched.

runSpeedMetersPerSecond.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): Vandal base run speed 5.4 m/s; the same value is in https://valorant.fandom.com/wiki/Vandal (docs/VALORANT-WEIGHTS.md section 2).

walkSpeedMetersPerSecond.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): walk = 0.55 x run speed = 2.97 m/s.

crouchSpeedMetersPerSecond.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): crouch = 0.3 x run speed = 1.62 m/s.

accel.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): ground acceleration 18 m/s^2 while a movement key is held. Riot publishes no movement constants.

friction.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): friction 3.3 per second on the velocity part against the key (turning, counter-strafe). Riot publishes no movement constants.

brakingFriction.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): braking friction 21.5 per second without a movement key. Riot publishes no movement constants.

frictionMin.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): minimum braking deceleration 11 m/s^2 without a movement key. Riot publishes no movement constants.

aboveMaxSpeedDecay.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): a speed above the top speed decays at 13 m/s^2. Riot publishes no movement constants.

walkAccelFactor.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): walk state scales the acceleration by 0.55. Riot publishes no movement constants.

walkBrakingFactor.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): walk state scales the braking friction by 0.55. Riot publishes no movement constants.

crouchAccelFactor.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): crouch state scales the acceleration by 0.4. Riot publishes no movement constants.

crouchFrictionFactor.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): crouch state scales the friction by 0.8. Riot publishes no movement constants.

crouchFrictionMinFactor.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied): crouch state scales the minimum braking deceleration by 0.85. Riot publishes no movement constants.

travelMeters.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied), tools/openaim-extract over 20 scenes with strafing bots (30 bots): way per strafe leg p10 1.0 m, p50 1.5 m, p90 1.75 m (timings.strafe_travel_s in valorant-engagements.json; the key is named _s but open-aim's strafe behaviour treats travel as a width in meters). The speed comes from the movement block.

dwellSeconds.source: open-aim commit 807f557 (github.com/unkwsr/open-aim, read only, no code copied), tools/openaim-extract over 20 scenes with strafing bots (30 bots): pause between legs p10 0.21 s, p50 0.33 s, max 0.65 s (timings.strafe_dwell_s).

reverseProbability.source: Assumption kept from docs/RANGE.md (Behaviour spec): open-aim's bots swing between two sides, so most legs turn around.

maxOffsetMeters.source: Assumption kept from docs/RANGE.md: the opponent stays within 2 m of its spawn, so a leg of up to 1.75 m always fits.
